judgment.notes: Torus length 2pi and normalized measure match the original; T remains a time parameter.
Fourier normalization, integer domain and distributional extension are explicit.
Sobolev completions, homogeneous mean-zero norms, reality, sequence norms and time-norm conventions match the standing context; no flow bound is granted by this definition.
Airy multiplier has the original positive Fourier phase; it defines an operator without assuming any solution property.
Mean is the zero Fourier coefficient, valid also for distributions.
Nonzero-mode projection is exactly I-P0; it does not impose a frequency cutoff.
Inverse derivative removes the zero mode and divides only at nonzero integers.
Second inverse derivative is a well-defined composition of D007.
Quadratic increment has the original two coefficients, projections and signs. L2 inputs have H1 inverse derivatives, making the products well-defined.

All four cubic increment terms match the original, including both endpoint signs and the 1/(27 tau) coefficient. tau>0 is explicit; inverse derivatives and H1 products make every term meaningful for L2 inputs.
Finite recursion starts at the given datum and includes all grid points; tau>0 is its domain restriction and tau=T/L is used under H001. No existence or convergence of an exact flow is assumed.
Step average has the explicit positive-step and integrability domains needed for division and integration.
Covariance is defined for arbitrary real phases using integrable exponentials; no estimate is inserted as a definition.

Finite polynomial convolution has zero output at k=0, excludes a+b=0, and uses exactly the original phases and prefactor. The definition explicitly withholds a bounded extension, exported separately by N004.
Sorted four-frequency magnitudes include the dual frequency; nonzero inputs ensure a positive third entry. Ties do not change its value.
pstar is exactly 23/14; inequalities involving it remain mathematical claims.
B is distributionally meaningful: L2 factors give an L1 product followed by a derivative and the Airy multiplier. No L2 product estimate is assumed.
Both inverse derivatives and the nonzero projection are explicit. H1 inverse derivatives make the product meaningful for the stated mean-zero L2 arguments.
The trilinear time integral is initially defined on smooth inputs; rough-input interpretation is expressly contingent on the continuous estimates, exported by N005.

X records the two specified norms and distributional time derivative. For the continuous finite-piece smooth functions actually used, no jump masses occur; membership and estimates remain proof obligations.
The three gamma cases, including the fixed 1/8 endpoint choice, are exhaustive under its explicit H001 guard; no product or stage estimate is granted.

The constant-input quadratic stage has the required 1/2 coefficient and step interval. In actual uses its mean-zero input lies in B's L2 domain (initially smooth); the integral is at least distributional, and stronger bounds are exported results.
z is only f plus the quadratic stage, with its step and input inherited from D022.
Cubic step integral is defined on smooth mean-zero inputs, with the time and frozen input explicitly specified.
Quartic stage is the smooth integral with coefficient 1/2 and the same quadratic stage in both slots.
W is the sum of the quartic endpoint and exact cubic remainder, with positive step and smooth input. Smooth Fourier sums give its meaning; the rough bounded extension is not assumed.
Interpolation is defined stepwise on smooth inputs with positive tau. Agreement of adjacent pieces and agreement with the scheme are explicitly left to N007.
Y is the difference of the interpolation and quadratic stage for the same step input; no smallness or regularity gain is assumed.
Residual increment has both bilinear integrals and the negative linear endpoint correction. It inherits the smooth step setting and positive tau from its stages; it grants no residual bound.

Concatenation is a finite sum with zero initial residual and the stage input v^j at each step. rho_j(t_j)=0 directly from D029 makes overlapping endpoint values consistent; all quantitative claims are exported separately.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
